intent: A menu row that turns one independent setting on or off.
typical_uses: A view setting kept in the menu, such as showing hidden files or a grid

dont_use_when.situation: One choice out of several mutually exclusive options
A one-off command with no on or off state
A setting that belongs to a form on the page
A setting that takes effect immediately, shown on the page rather than in a menu

invariants.text: `checked` and `defaultChecked` are both accepted; `defaultChecked` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `checked` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
Activating the row flips its state, reports it through `onCheckedChange` and leaves the menu open, unless `closeOnClick` is true.
A check glyph, hidden from assistive technology, is rendered at the row's inline end only while the item is checked; the row always reserves padding on its right side for it.
A `disabled` row stays in arrow-key navigation and can take focus, but pressing it or pressing Enter on it does nothing.

context-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the row to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking or taking pointer events, so a leading icon passed in children needs no size of its own.
`inset` indents the item's text by the width of the icon column (the small icon size plus two spacing steps), so it lines up with rows that start with an icon.

a11y.by: context-menu.test.tsx asserts the item is found by role menuitemcheckbox and its accessible name, and that clicking it calls onCheckedChange with true while the menu stays open; the primitive's Menu.CheckboxItem wires aria-checked

onCheckedChange.states: onCheckedChange is a callback called with the next checked state and event details, not a value
onCheckedChange.because: `(checked: boolean, eventDetails) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called with the click event when the row is activated by pointer or keyboard
onClick.because: A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the checkbox item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the checkbox item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, highlighted). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ContextMenuCheckboxItem with a fixed check icon; the kit exports no indicator to replace or place.

good.title: An uncontrolled setting that closes the menu when toggled

bad.title: A made-up onChange handler for the toggle
bad.why: The item has no `onChange`; the name falls through to the forwarded `<div>`, which fires no change event, so the checked value never updates. Use `onCheckedChange`.
